risks: Minimal: a 20-minute survey. The main risks are re-identification of nurses on small units or night shifts and use of the results against individuals.
consent: An information sheet on the tablet explains the purpose, the linkage to shift staffing and the reporting rule; completion implies consent, and nurses may skip any item or stop.
data: Responses are held by the research office, not by managers; after linkage the shift date is deleted; cells with fewer than five responses are suppressed in every report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: licensed practical nurses, night and part-time staff and internationally educated nurses may be under-represented or misunderstood by an instrument not validated for them. Paid time is offered on every shift, the checklist is pretested with licensed practical nurses, and response is reported by role and shift. For patients, dependent older adults and people with limited English are most affected by missed talk and teaching.
effectiveness: Informs the budget round with a measure both sides accept; a null association after acuity adjustment is equally informative.
efficiency: About 190 paid nursing hours and existing extracts.
costs: Paid survey time under the union agreement; analyst time within existing roles.
partnerships: A joint steering group of two union representatives, two unit managers and two patient partners agrees the checklist wording and the reporting rule.
rebPath: Approved by the hospital REB as minimal risk (REB-26-1182); ICH-GCP and Declaration of Helsinki principles for confidentiality apply.
limitations: Self-report of missed care; acuity as a unit mean; one hospital; winter only.
summary: Minimal-risk survey under REB approval with a non-blaming reporting rule agreed with the union and management.
